subject: gk
question: Select the INCORRECT statement of the following.

options.text: Vitamin C facilitates absorption and utilisation of iron in the body.
Vitamin C plays an important role in collagen synthesis.
Vitamin A, E and C act as antioxidants.
Fat is considered as a good source of energy during the exercise and competition.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Fat is considered as a good source of energy during the exercise and competition**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Fat is not considered a primary source of energy during exercise and competition; carbohydrates are preferred due to their quicker energy release.
 
• During high-intensity exercise, the body primarily relies on glycogen stored in muscles and liver for energy.
 
• Fat metabolism requires more oxygen and takes longer, making it less efficient as a source of immediate energy during exercise.
 
• Fat is utilized as a significant energy source during prolonged, low-intensity activities when carbohydrate reserves are depleted.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Role of Vitamin C:** Vitamin C enhances iron absorption by reducing ferric iron (Fe3+) to ferrous iron (Fe2+), which is more readily absorbed in the intestines.
 
• **Collagen Synthesis:** Vitamin C is essential in the hydroxylation of proline and lysine, which are critical steps in collagen formation.
 
• **Antioxidant Properties:** Vitamins A, E, and C act as antioxidants, neutralizing free radicals and protecting cells from oxidative damage.
 
• **Energy Sources During Exercise:** Carbohydrates are the main energy source for high-intensity exercise, while fats are utilized during prolonged, moderate-intensity activities.
 
• **Metabolic Differences:** Carbohydrate metabolism is anaerobic and faster, while fat metabolism is aerobic and slower but provides sustained energy for long-duration activities.
